_comment: Wave-5.5 furniture ratchet baseline. Regenerated by scripts/ratchet/check.sh's own recompute logic — see that script for the exact find/rg commands, and scripts/ratchet/process_globals.py for the fourth metric, which needs a scanner rather than a pattern. Do not hand-edit the counts without rerunning them; hand-edit only the metadata fields (computed_at_commit, computed_date, bump_reason) when intentionally moving the baseline.
bump_reason: Adds the sixth metric, raw_core_writes, at 0 (T48: raw writes to entities, type_index, the edge and short-id tables and sync_state outside batch/, ports/, store/, maintain/ and side_table/ went to 0). giant_files drops from 11 to 9 (batch/base_apply.rs and batch/put_apply/apply.rs are back under the bar); the baseline count stays 2 until T36. Previous bump reason: Adds the sixth metric, raw_core_writes, at 2 (T48 leg C: raw entities/type_index/edges_out/edges_in/short_ids/short_ids_reverse/sync_state writes outside batch/, ports/, store/, maintain/ and side_table/). Not yet 0: this leg's own hits (vault/transactions.rs's generic sync_state host doors, recovery/checkpoint/rebuild.rs) are fixed, but two hits in deletion/publish.rs belong to the concurrent maintenance-ports leg and are left for that leg to land; the count is a snapshot, not the post-merge value. No other counter moves. Previous bump reason: Adds the fifth metric, keyspace_census, at 0 (T47 typed keyspace: raw vault_meta calls outside side_table/, ports/ and store/open_gates/ went from 1743 at main ce8fd167 to 0). No other counter moves. Previous bump reason: Process globals 33 -> 34, measured by scripts/ratchet/process_globals.py. Codex 4054022149 exposed a causal-order regression in per-thread ULID minting. EntityId is a process-wide identity sequence consumed across vaults and threads, so its monotonic 128-bit state needs one mutex rather than vault- or thread-local ownership. No test-only global and no other counter increases. Previous baseline attribution is retained below.

giant_files.description: Non-test .rs files with >= 800 lines. Non-test = path has no 'tests/' directory component, filename is not 'tests.rs', does not end '_tests.rs' and does not start 'tests_'. vendor/ and target/ excluded.

_attribution.error_rs_left_2026_09_11: error.rs was the third file and is gone from the list. It was capped by one item, the 1436-line `pub enum Error`, and the attribution said clearing it meant decomposing `Error` into per-domain types - a semantic redesign, owner call. That call was made (ONE-2001, DESIGN-error-enum.md option B): the 21 cross-cutting variants stay flat on `Error`, the other 203 moved into twelve `#[error(transparent)]` domain enums, one file each under error/. error/mod.rs is 565 lines and the largest child, error/sync.rs, is 529. Variant names, `#[error(..)]` strings and `ErrorKind` are byte-identical; Debug gains one wrapper level for moved variants.
_attribution.correction_2026_09_09: The earlier claim that four of the remaining files were ordinary splittable modules was itself over-counted by one: pipeline/execution/channels.rs holds a single associated item, not several, so it was never cuttable per item. Single-function files are accepted; semantic streamlining is a separate pass.

No #[allow] or #[expect] was added anywhere; the root-surface pin held at 702.

The metric counts CLI output in a benchmark binary the same as a stray probe in library code; that is a limitation of the metric, not a regression in the tree.

process_global_statics.description: `static` items (including `static mut`) under crates/*/src whose DECLARED TYPE contains one of Mutex, RwLock, Atomic, OnceLock, OnceCell, LazyLock, 'Lazy<', 'Cell<', RefCell - or that REACHES one of them through a `type` alias or a named struct declared in the SAME file, so a global cannot duck the metric by being given a name. A static inside a `thread_local! { ... }` block is EXCLUDED (per-thread by definition). Test-gated (#[cfg(test)]) statics COUNT: under `cargo test --lib` sibling tests share one process, so a test-only global is exactly the seam that flakes. Non-test file = the same definition as giant_files (no 'tests/' path component, filename not tests.rs / *_tests.rs / tests_*.rs); vendor/ and target/ excluded. Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/process_globals.py; `--list` prints every hit as `path:line NAME: type`, with ` [via NAME]` naming the local alias or struct a resolved hit went through.

_attribution.summary: 38 -> 33 on 2026-09-11 (PR-2 of the per-vault ownership migration). Eight statics are gone and the scanner's alias gap is closed, which adds three that were always real. Every one of the 33 below is named with its bucket and its reason; there is no residue class left to work through.
_attribution.law: Engine state belongs to a vault (a field on StoreCore, the Arc-shared inner handle every Store and Vault reaches) or to a thread (thread_local!, when writer and reader are the same thread by construction). The process owns only locks that mirror an OS or LMDB rule, write-once registries and plugin doors, and monotonic id allocators. Every remaining static below is named with its bucket reason; a new one is a stated decision in its PR (AGENTS.md ratchet law).
_attribution.why_it_exists: Two flakes in one week came from process-global mutable state that tests read or arm. #922: the BM25 diagnostics counters are process-wide, so a sibling test in the same `cargo test --lib` binary moved them under a test that asserted on them. #923: the delete rendezvous slot is a single process-global Mutex, so two raced-delete tests clobbered each other's channel; the fix made that seam thread-local. PR-1 (#927) and PR-2 (#929) of the per-vault ownership migration moved or deleted every engine counter and test seam a vault could own; this counter now stops the class regrowing.

moved_to_storecore_7_2026_09_11.bm25/diagnostics.rs BM25_DIAGNOSTIC_COUN: -> bm25::Bm25Diagnostics, a StoreCore.diagnostics field. This is the #922 array itself; its tests dropped BM25_DIAGNOSTICS_TEST_LOCK and went back to exact deltas.
moved_to_storecore_7_2026_09_11.gate/decision.rs GATE_METRIC_COUNTERS: -> gate::GateMetrics, same field. The per-thread GATE_METRIC_EMISSIONS counter that proves a decision is not double-counted stays thread-local.
moved_to_storecore_7_2026_09_11.authority/first_seen_clock.rs LOCAL_CLOC: -> StoreCore.authority_local_clock: Mutex<AuthorityLocalClock>. It was a BTreeMap keyed by clock domain that grew per opened store and never shrank; the clock now dies with the handle.
moved_to_storecore_7_2026_09_11.store/open_gates/open_version_keys.rs NE: DELETED. It existed only to mint keys for LOCAL_CLOCKS. With the clock on the handle there is no key, so StoreCore::authority_clock_domain and StoreOwner's release-on-drop went with it.

pr2_2026_09_11.moved_onto_the_vault_3: deletion/rendezvous.rs DELETE_RENDEZVOUS (the #923 flake itself) and its AFTER_HEADER_READ thread-local, outbound_intent_ledger/store.rs FORCE_SYNC_CALLS, and batch/export/foreign_stage/export_foreign_stage.rs STAGED_IMPORT_PRE_CONTENT_HOOK -> fields on `#[cfg(test)] StoreCore.test_hooks`, reached as vault.test_hooks(). The scanner only ever counted two of the three: the pre-content hook was hidden behind the ArmedPreContentHook alias.
pr2_2026_09_11.locks_moved_onto_the_vault_2: batch/export/foreign_stage/export_foreign_stage.rs STAGED_IMPORT_ADMISSION_LOCK and sync/client/federated.rs STAGED_IMPORT_LOCK -> StoreCore.staged_import_admission_lock and .staged_import_confirm_lock, both production fields under #[cfg(feature = "sync")]. The design left these undecided pending evidence. Every row inside either critical section is addressed through the vault that owns it - the receipt row, the staged content row and the selector admission all go through `vault.store.sync_state` - so neither guards a shared host path, and a process-wide lock was serializing unrelated vaults for nothing.
pr2_2026_09_11.deleted_as_dead_4: identity_topology/shell_edge_reconcile.rs FULL_RECONCILIATIONS was incremented on every full reconcile and read by nobody; sync/client/federated.rs STOP_AFTER_STAGED_IMPORT and its two arming fns had no caller in any crate; export_foreign_stage.rs STAGED_IMPORT_ADMISSION_COUNT and STAGED_IMPORT_FIRST_STAGE_BARRIER likewise. A seam nothing reads is not state that needs an owner, and AGENTS.md deletes a helper with no remaining caller rather than keeping it.
pr2_2026_09_11.serial_lock_deleted: memory/tests/support.rs DELETE_RENDEZVOUS_TESTS and its seven lock_delete_rendezvous() holders are gone: the lock existed only because the rendezvous was one process-global slot, and a per-vault seam needs none. It never counted toward this metric (it lives under a tests/ path), but it is the cost the shared seam was imposing - seven raced-delete tests that had to run one at a time.
pr2_2026_09_11.scanner_alias_gap_closed: The metric read the DECLARED type, so an alias or a named struct hid a global from it. process_globals.py now resolves both when they are declared in the same file, and the three surviving known_gap_4_statics items are counted: store/test_hooks.rs BEFORE_LMDB_OPEN and AFTER_LMDB_OPEN (LmdbOpenHookSlot) and oneiron-remote/src/embedded.rs REGISTRY (a Registry struct holding an AtomicU32 and a LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap>>). The fourth, STAGED_IMPORT_PRE_CONTENT_HOOK, this PR deleted. Resolution is same-file and textual; a cross-file alias would still hide one, which is stated rather than guessed at.

split_33.resource_locks_6: Process-wide mutual exclusion over a process-wide resource. One LMDB env per path per process: store/open_gates/open_version_keys.rs:185 LMDB_DATABASE_OPEN_LOCK, :187 VAULT_ROOT_OPEN_LOCK and :189 OPEN_STORE_PATHS, all three of which fire before any Store exists, so no owner can hold them. Git repos on disk are process resources: git_wire/repo.rs:91 GIT_WIRE_REPO_LOCKS. One embedded vault per path per process, pid-guarded: oneiron-remote/src/embedded.rs:86 REGISTRY. One overflow probe at a time: oneiron-bench/src/perf/build_profile.rs:296 PROBE_HOOK.

Engine: agent_def/manifest.rs:287 MANIFEST, channel_identity_manifest.rs:164 MATRIX, edit_distance/routing/version.rs:20 MODEL_STACK_REGISTRY, git_wire/env.rs:29 GIT_WIRE_PROCESS_ENV, ingest/image.rs:91 RECOGNIZER and :92 CAPTION_RECOGNIZER, outbound/capability.rs:212 MANIFESTS, skill_optimize/gate/basis.rs:285 HELD_OUT_REPLAY_SCORER. Engine: repo_mutation/worktree.rs:18 REPO_MUTATION_WORKTREE_COUNTER, session_overlay/overlay/segment.rs:29 NEXT_OVERLAY_GENERATION. Server request/session ids: api/facade.rs:396 COUNTER, commands/api.rs:422 COUNTER, error.rs:555 REQUEST_ID_COUNTER, livequery/error.rs:24 COUNTER, server/lifecycle.rs:18 NEXT_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID.
split_33.host_process_caches_and_live_registries_: State whose SUBJECT is the server process, not a vault: one server answers many requests and holds one set of live connections. oneiron-server/src/api/booking/page_token.rs:76 MEMO, api/context_board/cursor.rs:19 MEMORIES_CURSOR_STORE, livequery/connection.rs:30 HUBS, oauth_relay.rs:40 JWKS_CACHE.
split_33.process_scoped_observation_1: oneiron-remote/src/embedded.rs:96 STORE_OPEN_COUNT. It counts the Vault::open calls THIS PROCESS made, which is the fact the same-pid-reopen-shares contract test asserts; per-vault it would be meaningless.
split_33.pre_store_test_hooks_2: store/test_hooks.rs:161 BEFORE_LMDB_OPEN and :168 AFTER_LMDB_OPEN. They fire between the vault root being bound and the LMDB environment being opened - before any Store exists to own them - and are path-keyed, so a hook armed by one test cannot fire inside another test's open. Newly counted here because the scanner now resolves their LmdbOpenHookSlot alias.
split_33.server_test_seam_1: oneiron-server/src/oauth_relay.rs:125 TEST_TRANSPORTS, a path-keyed map of stub transports. The only cfg(test) seam left on the list. It is a server concern, not an engine one: no vault owns an OAuth relay transport, and the server's own per-test isolation is a separate question from this migration.

_attribution.expected_direction: Flat. The engine class this migration existed for is closed: no #[cfg(test)] static remains under crates/oneiron/src that a vault could own. The seven survivors there are two pre-store hooks, three open-time resource locks, one repo-lock map and one process env, each named above. A new static is a stated decision in its PR (AGENTS.md ratchet law).
_attribution.w7_c06: EntityId::now LAST_ULID: one monotonic process-wide ULID mint sequence, preserving cross-thread newest-id projections. Regression uses channel handoffs, not a global test reset.

keyspace_census.description: Raw `vault_meta` calls (get, put, delete, prefix_iter, range, rev_range on any receiver, line breaks allowed around the dot) in non-test files under crates/oneiron/src, outside the three places that own the table: side_table/ (the typed keyspace door), ports/ and store/open_gates/ (the storage ABI and manifest handshake rows). Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/keyspace_census.py; `--list` prints every hit.

_attribution.summary: 1743 -> 0 (T47, Wave 8 plumbing). Every module's private rows moved onto typed tables declared once in crate::side_table (582 declarations, disjoint by a compile-time check); the copied MessagePack and JSON codecs and hand-spelled prefixes went with them.
_attribution.expected_direction: Zero. A module that needs a new row declares it in side_table/decls and binds a typed table; a raw call is a finding.

raw_core_writes.description: Raw `.put(`, `.delete(` and `.delete_range(` calls on the tables entities, type_index, edges_out, edges_in, short_ids, short_ids_reverse and sync_state (any receiver, `x.table.put(` or `x.table().put(`, line breaks allowed) in non-test files under crates/oneiron/src, outside the five places that own these tables: batch/ (the builders), ports/ (the storage ports), store/ (the storage ABI and manifest handshake rows), maintain/ (index upkeep) and side_table/ (T47's typed keyspace). Non-test here is check.sh's path rule PLUS a file reached only through a `#[cfg(test)] mod` declaration (directly or transitively) PLUS masking an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { .. }` body inside an otherwise-production file — keyspace_census.py does not need the last two because vault_meta prose rarely appears in inline test fixtures the way raw entity/edge/sync_state writes do. Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/raw_write_census.py; `--list` prints every hit.

_attribution.summary: T48 (Wave 8 plumbing): 164 raw core writes outside the doors at main ce8fd167 (module-aware rule) -> 0. Entity rewrites go through named EntityStoreMaintenance ports (the erase scrub, document pointers, the redaction receipt, the retained shell), the ARCH-0023b document families through the DocumentRowStore port, and every other sync_state row through T47's typed tables; the generic host sync_state doors on Vault write only under a declared table.
_attribution.expected_direction: Zero. A new raw write to these tables outside the doors is a finding.

_metric_definition_gap_found_2026_09_09: CLOSED 2026-09-09. The non-test exclusion matched 'tests.rs' and '*_tests.rs' but not 'tests_*.rs', a spelling the repo also uses (branch_store_oracle/tests_leak_sweep.rs, api/git_http/tests_auth.rs, oneiron-bench/beam/tests_*.rs and 15 more), so those 18 files counted as production. check.sh now excludes that spelling too, in both the ripgrep globs and the giant_files find pipeline. NO COUNT MOVED: those 18 files hold zero '#[allow(' and zero print macros and none reaches 800 lines. This closed a latent hole before it could report a test file as a production giant; it did not relax any number.
